title: airgap: add Ubuntu 22.04 slim runtime bundle, modular vendor indexer, and registry-sync TF updates
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in stricter regulated environments requested a smaller Ubuntu-based runtime bundle (22.04) optimized for constrained air-gapped environments and an improved, modular vendor indexer that supports incremental delta snapshots. This PR introduces a slim Ubuntu 22.04 runtime bundle profile, refactors the offline image index format to be modular (index shards + manifest), and updates the Terraform registry-replication module to optionally use the new index format for faster syncs and reduced bandwidth.

Summary of changes: added ubuntu-22.04-slim runtime bundle (compressed tar.gz, stripped docs, minimal kernel modules), implemented index-shard format v1 for the airgap indexer (index-manifest.json + shard-<n>.json), added dedupe layer to offline image packaging, updated Helm chart to expose registry-proxy.enabled and mirror.oci settings, extended the installer "airgap-apply" flow to accept --index-shard flag and to perform atomic apply using snapshot fencing. Terraform: added optional parameter "use_index_shards" and optimized S3 upload concurrency for large delta snapshots. Rollback/upgrade: introduced preflight checks and a new rollback hook that validates bundle signature before applying a rollback.

How to test locally: follow docs/airgap/ubuntu-22.04/README.md (included). Example: ./bin/airgap-tool build --profile ubuntu-22.04-slim --index-shard-size 200MB && ./bin/airgap-tool pack --output /tmp/airgap-slim.tar.gz. Deploy to a k3s lab cluster with registry-mirror enabled and run ./scripts/e2e/airgap-sync.sh. CI includes an airgap-registry-indexer-e2e job that exercises shard creation and registry replication.

Upgrade notes: upgrade path is backwards compatible. Default behaviour remains the monolithic index unless --use-index_shards=true is set. For customers using the Dedicated registry replication Terraform module, enabling shards can reduce peak bandwidth but requires the newer airgap-tool >= 0.28.0. Please follow the migration checklist in docs/airgap/migration.md.

Checklist: - [x] Add ubuntu-22.04-slim bundle recipe and packaging pipeline - [x] Implement index-shard manifest and shard creation tools - [x] Helm changes for registry-proxy and mirror settings - [x] Terraform module parameter and docs - [x] E2E test for shard-based replication - [x] Package signing and verification step added

Related work: builds on prior airgap improvements (see SUP-1337 and ENG-6120) and complements the offline delta snapshot work in ENG-5830.

Notes: kept the new index format intentionally simple (manifest + shards) so on-prem mirrored registries can stream shards sequentially and resume. The packaging script also deduplicates blobs across bundles which reduced typical bundle size by ~12% in our benchmark sample.

release_notes: Add a new Ubuntu 22.04 slim airgap bundle profile, modular index shard format for faster incremental syncs, Helm support for registry-proxy and OCI mirror settings, Terraform registry-replica improvements, and new rollback signature verification hook.
notes_for_ops: Operators enabling shard-based replication should ensure airgap-tool >= 0.28.0 and set S3 endpoint lifecycle rules to keep shard manifests for the expected window. If using on-prem S3-compatible storage, enable range requests for shard downloads.
why_unique: Focuses on a slim Ubuntu 22.04 runtime bundle + a simple modular index shard format and a Terraform optimization path; different distro (Ubuntu 22.04) and shard-based strategy distinct from existing monolithic index and other distro-specific PRs.
